newsitem.title: CHINA: China considers BOT financing for waterworks.
newsitem.headline: China considers BOT financing for waterworks.

text.p: Beijing is considering the introduction of build-operate-transfer (BOT) financing for water supply projects to help slake the thirst of some of China's parched cities, the China Daily said on Thursday.

China favoured using BOT financing for water-related infrastructure to lighten the financial burden of construction, the official newspaper quoted vice-minister of water resources Zhang Chunyuan as saying.
Under BOT financing a private investor pays to build a project in return for the right to operate it for a fixed period, after which control is turned over to the state.
Hundreds of Chinese cities suffer from chronic water shortages, prompting calls for infrastructure projects to move water to dry areas.

The Ministry of Water Resources was considering a batch of pilot BOT projects and had drawn up draft laws and rules on such projects and submitted them for approval, the China Daily said but gave no details.
BOT financing could be complicated because it involved a wide range of legislative, financial and technological issues, it quoted Zhang as saying.

China's State Council, or cabinet, has been considering BOT rules aimed at boosting the use of BOT financing in the key power industry. Officials are also hoping to attract BOT financing to highway construction projects around the country.
